findings.text: follow-on: the enforcement path has no covering test. LaneHeld is declared (3568) and raised once (5616), and no test anywhere in the tree references LaneHeld (grep -rn LaneHeld tests/ -> empty). The new cases stop at _lane_worker_allowance's held flag, so the raise that actually holds the node, and the surfaces that must report it as a lane-paused hold, are unverified by this node's own gate. The plan's done-when asks only for the rule to be driven, so this is not a blocking gap, but a regression that removed the raise would leave every new test green.

follow-on (the reviewed manifest's own follow_on 2, confirmed): change_lane() resolves the destination through plan_dispatch without session=, and change_lane takes no session argument, so a re-resolved allowance sees session_id "", is never listed in the sessions map, and falls to new_session_worker_slots in place of the coordinator session's own share. The two in-dispatch() resolution sites (5419, 5541) do pass session. Outside this node's fence.

follow-on (the reviewed manifest's own follow_on 1, confirmed): test_no_dispatch_is_refused_held_or_rerouted_by_any_value_in_the_document drives a zero-headroom document with no admission block and asserts the dispatch is not held. That doctrine is now false for the real path — this review drove the same document through _lane_worker_allowance and got allowance 0.0, held True — but the test passes because it drives a dry run (_arguments default dry_run=True) that never reaches the raise. The case should be re-cut when the hold is next touched.

justifications.durability: The rule lives in product source and the covering test fails when it is reverted — proved by the negative control this review reproduced. The tests drive every rung through the lane reader's own path (read_lane_document + read_lane_admission), so the rule is exercised as production resolves it. The weaker point is that the enforcement half — the LaneHeld raise at dispatch.py:5616 that actually holds the node — has no covering test: the new cases assert the decision's held flag but never that dispatch() raises, so a regression that dropped the raise while keeping the decision would stay green. Noted as a follow-on.
justifications.evidence: Both arms are complete and readable: base c47424bd 1128 passed / 2 skipped EXIT=0, head d6d3173d1 1136 passed / 2 skipped EXIT=0, logged verbatim in the reviewed manifest's baseline_suite/after_suite and in gate-base.log / gate-head.log with full headers (revision, tree, cwd, module_file, command) and a bare EXIT= line. The negative control is genuine: EXIT=1 with four failing ids including the required positive per-session case. This review independently re-ran the new file at the reviewed head (8 passed, EXIT=0) and reproduced the declared headroom-only mutation in a fresh scratch tree (4 failed, EXIT=1, same first id). Deducted for two provenance gaps rather than missing arms: the head arm ran at d6d3173d1 while the node head is 2a9435b0b (docs-only delta), and the reviewed manifest records commits d6d3173d1/2a9435b0b plus a live control, so the count is well-founded.
justifications.fit: read_lane_admission sits beside read_lane_counts in lane_document.py with its key constants named ADMISSION_*; the dispatch side adds one private helper pair (_lane_worker_allowance / _dispatch_lane_allowance) beside the existing lane readers and one DispatchPlan field; LaneHeld subclasses LanePaused rather than opening a parallel refusal family; no version suffixes and no plan identifiers in symbols. Docstrings state the mechanism (the router's own preference, the filling observation window) rather than the incident.
justifications.goal_fidelity: reckon/crew/dispatch.py:5190-5291 (_lane_worker_allowance) resolves the allowance in the router's own order — the session's own worker_slots when the sessions map lists it, new_session_worker_slots when the map is present and does not, the global worker_slots, then headroom read as a worker count — and disables every slot rung until the block reports at >=900 s of observation, holding on the request duty cycle rather than the request count. An allowance of zero or less raises LaneHeld (subclass of LanePaused) at dispatch.py:5616 before any pointer or worktree exists, naming the router's verdict; an unreadable allowance holds nothing. This is §11's four-rung order, its 900 s distrust and its held-on-zero rule, with no fairness arithmetic of reckon's own. Read live at 2026-10-02T06:33:11Z, session s22-coord resolved to 5 beside headroom 4, held false (the log in the run dir).
